جَاشِرِيَّةٌ (tropical:) A drink that is taken at daybreak: (S, A, K:) you say, اِصْطَبَحْنَا الجَاشِرِيَّةَ We drank the morning-draught that is taken at daybreak: (S, A:) and it has no verb: (S:) or it is only of camels' milk: (K:) or it is correctly of general application: or is properly of wine; for this is what is most frequently mentioned: and it is also used as an epithet: thus you say شَرْبَةٌ جَاشِرِيَّةٌ (TA.) ―
-b2- (assumed tropical:) A certain kind of food: (K, TA:) or a kind of food eaten at daybreak. (TA.) ―
-b3- (assumed tropical:) The [last part of the night, called the] سَحَر: (K:) because near to daybreak. (TA.) ―
-b4- (assumed tropical:) Midday: (K:) because of the appearance and spreading of its light. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
